utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Spahic, we left off yesterday with one of my questions which I'm going to repeat now, and that is the following: Do you remember the time that the convoy left Visegrad, the convoy that you yourself were in?

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was sometime between 10.30 and 11.00. I couldn't be specific as to the time, but it was around half past 10.00 or 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did the whole convoy start at that time? Were you able to notice? Did all the vehicles making up the convoy start at the same time?

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume they did. I didn't actually pay attention but I think they did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the convoy started its journey across the new bridge on the Drina River; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said you were surprised because you took that route across that particular bridge. I'm sure you know that the old bridge or the Turkish bridge is not -- does not cater to heavy traffic for trucks and buses.

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I wasn't surprised that we were going across the new bridge, but I was surprised because we said we wanted to be taken to Skopje and that would mean going through town. And, in fact, we did go through town but then we took a turn towards the new bridge, which was unusual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. Domazet. Sir, because you and Mr. Domazet, the counsel there, are talking the same language, you present a problem with the interpretation. After he's asked his question, would you just pause a moment to enable the interpreters to catch up? Because we are getting it in English and French as well, you see, so just pause just like Mr. Domazet pauses before the question. I'm sorry, Mr. Domazet. You proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I understand why you were surprised. So you were surprised because of the direction you took across the new bridge and not because you didn't go across the old bridge, which you knew you couldn't. You said that in your particular bus, the bus you were in, that there were two guards and that you knew one of them and that he was a waiter from Visegrad whom you knew. Could you describe him to us, please?

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a young man, had a dark complexion. He was good-looking and pleasant. I knew him very well, but I can't recall his name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very soon after the tragic events that came to pass - that is to say, several months later - you made a statement to the MUP, and you said that the waiter's name was Brane Ivanovic. You named the waiter. Do you remember his name now?

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's another waiter. It's a different waiter, a waiter that I came into contact with at Sokolac. It wasn't the same one. And I know that second waiter. I knew his name. And it's quite a different waiter altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Recounting what you personally experienced and all the events that took place, you gave a number of statements to MUP and a statement to the investigator of the OTP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In none of those statements do you make mention of the name Mitar Vasiljevic, who is on trial here today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERID SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Ossogo?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir. That is the end of your task here. We are very Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. grateful to you for having come to give evidence and for the evidence which you've given. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, welcome back to the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm afraid it's only a guest appearance.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You must turn your microphone on. You're taking VG14, are you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am. He's been given protective measures, as I understand it. Can I hand the sheet to Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have got the pseudonym sheet?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have, which is going to be handed to Your Honour now. Your Honour, in the absence of the witness, may I explain that I've spoken to Mr. Domazet, and I understand that there is no dispute about the events until one comes to the river and, therefore, he's agreed I may lead the witness on the earlier part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank heaven's that we are going to have some leading because there is very little in dispute about the earlier matters here. This pseudonym sheet for the witness VG14 will be Exhibit 73, and it is under seal: Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, would you please make the solemn declaration in the document which the usher is showing you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please sit down, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I wonder if you could have a look please at a sheet which has been marked Exhibit number 73?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it in front of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Doesn't appear to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Something slipped up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see your name there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Throughout these proceedings, however, you will be referred to as Witness VG14. You will see on the sheet another name. If you wish to refer to him, he should be referred to as VG32. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I want to ask you first of all a little bit about your background. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you're now aged 34?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it's right that after you left school, you did your JNA compulsory training between 1987 and 1988.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And just to jump forward for a moment, I think after the events that you're going to tell us about, you in fact joined the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you briefly about the events after the multi-party system elections in 1990. Did you first notice that there were ethnic tensions in Visegrad after those elections?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did those tensions eventually lead to the beginning of what you call the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In around March or April of 1992, did the Uzice Corps enter Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. That was at the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as a result of that, did you leave the area of Visegrad in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, eventually, did you return because you were told that you would be safe to return to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At that stage, were you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you have children? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, a three and a half year old daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you returned to the area of Visegrad in which you lived, did you notice that there had been damage done to property there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What kind of damage did you notice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Houses were burnt down. There was looting of houses and property.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you also stopped on your return at a number of checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. There were several checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who were those checkpoints manned by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The checkpoints belonged to the former JNA, and they were manned by the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The uniform that the soldiers were wearing, was it regular JNA uniform or did it have other markings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, there were the olive-grey green uniforms and the camouflage uniforms and, generally speaking, the JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I wonder if we could just clear one point up. He talked about the war or the Uzice Corps entering at the beginning of April, and then you asked a question did you -- eventually did you return because were you told that it would be safe to return. Was that whilst the Uzice Corps was still there or after they left? It may or may not be important, but it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When did you return to the area of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: It was some ten days after the entrance of the Uzice Corps in Visegrad. So the Uzice Corps was actually in Visegrad when I came back to Visegrad myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So roughly what date are we talking about for the return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but I think it was towards the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, after your return, were you able to continue working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: When I came back to Visegrad, I continued working in my firm. But it wasn't safe, because people were already being taken away from the firm, so that one month later I had to leave the company I worked for.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So can we take it this was sometime in May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, other than the Uzice Corps, were there other military formations in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. There were the White Eagles, as they were called.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who exactly were the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: They are -- the White Eagles included local Serbs. So it wasn't just the White Eagles themselves imported, as we used to say, but the local Serbs formed part of the White Eagles as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How were you able to differentiate between the regular Uzice Corps and the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The members of the regular Uzice Corps had the insignia of the former JNA, whereas the White Eagles had different insignia with a double-headed eagle on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What kind of activities were the White Eagles carrying out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: As far as I was able to notice, they did what they wanted to. They weren't under anybody's control.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you say they did what they wanted to, can you just give us one or two examples of what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, I can. One of their checkpoints was situated in front of the new hotel in Visegrad, so they controlled all the traffic in front of the hotel. The second example is that they stormed houses and apartments at any time during the day and night and they would take away the people that they had on their lists from those places.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how did you find out about the people who were on the lists? Or I'm sorry, I'll rephrase the question. How did you find out that they had lists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: A good example is this: Going to work and coming back from work, I saw that they had these lists at the checkpoints, and they would look at the lists, check the list when they looked at my ID cards. They would look at me, look down the list and then say, "Well, he's not on the list. He can be allowed to pass."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I should have asked you this before, and it is my error. What was your -- what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did the Uzice Corps leave Visegrad at the end of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But did the White Eagles remain in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were there any regular JNA army corps left in the town after the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Uzice left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't actually see that or recognise that, but I know that the White Eagles were left and they were joined by the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, after you'd stopped working, did you in fact go into hiding near your flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, eventually, did you get tired of hiding and did you go back to live in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about the day that you were arrested. Can you remember what day that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was a Saturday, the 7th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That afternoon, were you in your flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was your wife and your child -- were your wife and your child there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were there also some friends of yours there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. They had been expelled from the village of Kurtalici.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who came to your flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: That afternoon, Milan Lukic and another man came to the flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Milan Lukic, had you known him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, from our school days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: For how long had you known him therefore by June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, seven years about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When he came to your flat, you said he was with someone else. Do you know who that man was? Had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No. That was the first time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: All I heard was that he called him Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That was Lukic calling him Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was Lukic wearing when he came to your flat that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He was wearing a blue beret with the double-headed eagle insignia, a camouflage uniform, and white trainers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did he have any insignia on that uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. On the left-hand side, on the pocket, he had the double-headed eagle emblem, and on his hand, he had a plaster, elastoplast.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you know what Lukic was doing in June of 1992, what his job, if any, was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He came from Obrenovac. I think he worked there as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us he had a plaster on his hand. Did you notice anything else about him, about his face, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He was sooty, and on one half of his face, I can't remember what exactly, but I think he had a mole of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: By sooty, do you mean that it looked as though he had gone through dust, or did it look as though it was deliberate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think it was deliberate, to mask himself, camouflage himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, when he got to your flat, how did he come in? In other words, did he knock on the door, or what did he do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, when he came to my flat, he knocked on the door, and I asked my neighbour, a woman, to tell him that there was nobody at home, nobody in the flat. However, when she saw what he looked like, I suppose she was afraid, and couldn't answer anything. After that, he forced his way into the flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What did he tell you when he came into the flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He asked me what my name was, and I told him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you surprised by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you told him your name, and then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He came into the flat and started ransacking it, searching it. He found my uniform belonging to the reserve force of the JNA. He told me to take the uniform and to follow him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did he give you any explanation why you had to go with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At that stage, what did you expect was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I thought that he might detain me somewhere or exchange me for one of his own people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What led you to believe that? In other words, from what experiences did you think that that might happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The confidence and trust in the former JNA -- I always had confidence and trust in the JNA, and I couldn't imagine a day when that wouldn't be so and when the people would have been affected by it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You said you had trust in the JNA, but what was the situation like Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in June when Milan Lukic came to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. At that time, the JNA was no longer there, and I probably no longer had their trust -- that trust. I don't know when I lost it, actually. I don't know how to explain this to you. There was an army that guaranteed your security, and now all of a sudden some people came and took away whoever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This type of incident, had that happened to people that you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So he told you to follow -- to go with him. What happened to your wife and child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: My wife and child remained at the door, at the entrance to the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to say goodbye to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I was not allowed to do that by Lukic. However, of my own free will, I went back to kiss my daughter and to kiss my wife because I felt that this might be my last day with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you had seen people who had been evicted from the village of Kurtalici. What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Those people were there. One of them was also taken with me on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: That was Amir Kurtalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So when you left your apartment, there were four of you: Milan Lukic, yourself, Amir, and this man Montenegro; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where did you go once you had left the apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: We got into a car, a Passat, that Milan Lukic had taken from Behija Zukic, and we went to another place in Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that the car was taken from someone. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. People talked about that, and they said that Milan Lukic on one night got into Behija Zukic's apartment, killed her, and took her car.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you know the lady who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what colour was the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The colour? It was dark red. It was maroon, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, before you and Amir got into the car, did Lukic do or say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. He prayed the way Muslims pray to God. He said "Bismillah".

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did he explain why he was doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you got into the car and where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: We went back towards Visegrad but not far away from my apartment. We entered the neighbouring street where there were other arrested Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where did you see the other arrested Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: As we got into the street, one of his soldiers was guarding them in a house, and he took them out of that house. There were four other men there too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I think this is right: Is one of the men -- one of the men was the one who you will be referring to as (redacted); is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the names of the other men, please, though?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, Meho Dzafic, Ekrem Dzafic, (redacted), Hasan Kustura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I thought you had been invited to lead all the way up to the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, Your Honour. I thought that might be important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may or may not. We have got most of them already. But if there is no dispute until we get to the river, let's get there, if we could.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Once -- what happened to the men who were -- who came out of the house? Were they put into your car or into another car as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. Another car was there, a Yugo, a grey Yugo. And one of these men was transferred to our car; and that was [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then were you taken to a place called Visegradska Banja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour I don't know whether it would assist if at this stage the witness identifies these places on a map. I don't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. know whether Your Honours have had a chance to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We've had a very large map shown us. It blocked the view of the interpreters for sometime. Unless you really think it's important, we have had the map, not marked; we have had them noted on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honour, I won't trouble you with it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you taken there to a hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At the hotel -- I'm sorry, just one thing. Before you got to the hotel, were you stopped at a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. This was the checkpoint at Sase where Lukic said to these men at the checkpoint that he had caught some balijas.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did Lukic also ask you whether you had any money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That was as we were leaving my apartment and going towards Visegrad. I answered him that I had about two billion, and he said, "You mean German marks?" And I said, "No, old Bosnian money."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, once at the hotel, were you taken into the reception area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At that stage, did Lukic start to look for the keys to an office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. He was asking for the keys of the manager's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whilst he was doing that, did you see other people there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. Mitar Vasiljevic was there. He was standing in the immediate vicinity, and Momir Savic was at the entrance into the Vilina Vlas hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, for how long had you known him in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, for about ten years.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In what capacity had you known him? In other words, as a friend or a colleague or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. Mitar Vasiljevic worked as a waiter in Panos where I stayed quite often, so I could knew him -- could know him quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you be able to recognise him again today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I would like you to look around the court, please, then, and see if you can identify him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. It's the gentleman there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you just -- I'm afraid for the purposes of the record, we need a slightly more clear identification. Which gentleman are you describing? You've pointed at somebody.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: That dark-haired man there in the last row with head set on his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There is no doubt that that must be the accused person.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was he wearing when you saw him in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He was wearing a black hat, an olive-green/grey uniform with a band on his shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there any kind of insignia? The band you describe, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, it was a red band and on the hat, he also had an emblem; the two-headed eagle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did he have anything with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. He had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How do you know that it was an automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I did my military service, and one year must have been sufficient for me to get to know the weapons that I also carried then in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When Milan Lukic came to your apartment, did he have a weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. He had a sniper with a silencer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And by sniper, you mean rifle, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The other man there that you'd mentioned, Momir Savic, did he have any weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Also an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, apart from Savic and Vasiljevic, did you see anybody else there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. The former watch-keeper of that hotel was there too. His last name was Susnjar, but I can't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he in civilian clothes or in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He also had an olive-green/grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did he have a weapon? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, a semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that Lukic was looking for keys. Did he find the keys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, he found some keys. And he tried to open the manager's office with those keys, but he didn't manage to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And so eventually, were you ordered back into the cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you in the same car, the Passat, the Volkswagen, that you had come to the hotel in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened to the three new men that you've described; Vasiljevic, first of all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, Vasiljevic then joined Milan Lukic, and he got into the same car where I was; that is to say, the Passat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the other two people? Momir Savic, did he come with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No, he stayed at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Susnjar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He did too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So there is Lukic and Vasiljevic and you and Amir in the first car, in the Volkswagen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, and Hasan Mutapcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the other car that you've talked about, the Yugo, how many people apart from the arrested people that you've named were in that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: There were six people; that is to say, four people who were arrested and two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: They took us in the direction of Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you get to Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And where did the cars stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The cars stopped in front of a house. Mitar Vasiljevic, as he was talking to Lukic, said that this was a Muslim house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When the cars stopped, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: They ordered us to get out of the car and told us not to try to escape.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you remember now who gave the orders? You've told us that Lukic and Vasiljevic were in the car with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. This order was issued by Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So did you get out of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did Amir get out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. We all got out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Once you were outside the car, what was said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: We were told to start walking towards the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Roughly how far was the Drina from where the car had stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think about a hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us you were ordered to walk towards the Drina. How did you walk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: We walked in a column, one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whilst you were doing that, where were Lukic and Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think that I said quite precisely in my statement that they were on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the other two men who were -- the other two soldiers who were with the other car? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: They were on the other side, so we didn't have a chance to run either one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As you walked down to the river, what did you think was going to happen to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. That is the right moment to feel that there would be a tragedy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you -- when you say, "That was the right moment to feel there was a tragedy," can you just elaborate, please, a little? What did you think was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, yes, I couldn't think of anything else but that these were the last moments of my life and that there were only a few metres to the river, and that is what divided me from my death.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Feeling that, did you or any of the others, attempt to run away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, we wouldn't stand a chance of doing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened when you got to the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: When we got to the river, we were lined up facing the water. The Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. soldiers were about five or six metres behind us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At that stage, what was the level of the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. As for the level of the river, it was going down because the lake had changed its level, so you could also see part of the bank itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you were told to line up facing the river. Did anybody say anything to any of the four men who you told us had weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. Meho Dzafic, Mitar Vasiljevic's colleague, who worked in the same company as Mitar did, he begged him not to kill him, because they were colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did Vasiljevic make any response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. He said that he didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you lined up on the bank of the river, were you facing the river, or facing the men who were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I've already said that I was facing the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: A question followed: "How should we shoot, individual gunshots or bursts of gunfire?"

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember who asked that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think it was Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He asked how they should shoot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anybody give a reply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Somebody replied that they should fire individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: A click was heard of the weapons when they were being adjusted from bursts of gunfire to individual shots, and then shots followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before the shots, did you hear anybody give an order to fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How many shots did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Four shots. There were three stronger ones and one was a blunt one, that is to say a sniper rifle with a silencer and that sound is muffled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've told us that Vasiljevic had an automatic weapon. The other two men with weapons, what kind were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: They all had automatic weapons except for Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I'm sorry if I've asked you this already. Yes, I have, for give me. I've asked you how many shots. What did you do as the shots went off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. Until the present day now, when I'm here, I cannot think of how I managed to do this. It's as if God himself had saved me, as if someone had pushed me into that river, and it so happened that I survived.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, pushed you into the river? Did you fall into the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't mean that anybody had pushed me. I said as if there were a power that had pushed me. I fell into the water pretending to be dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the other men with you? Did you notice any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, I heard them fall into the water. I couldn't tell who it was at that stage. However, I did hear other falls into the water.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see any of the other men while you were in the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. When all of this was over, a person who also survived, that is person number 32, I noticed that this person was alive as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Before you noticed that, however, you'd heard the shots, you fell in the water. What was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The next thing that happened? I heard the screams of one of these men. He was probably wounded. Another gunshot followed and then the screams stopped. That meant that that man had been killed too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The men who had fired the shots, did any of them come closer to the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. When all of this was over, somebody walked up to the water and said, "One of them is alive."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you able to say who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So he said one of them was alive. And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Three gunshots followed. Two were aimed at my head and they missed, and the third one went further, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then what happened to the men with guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Sometime after that, we heard the cars being ignited and that meant that they were leaving.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Then I lifted my head, looked around and returned to the same position that I had been in.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which was where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Could you please repeat this question? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You said you returned to the same position that you had been in. Do you mean that you remained in the water or that you got out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I stayed in the water for another minute or two perhaps because I still could not believe that these soldiers had left. I was afraid that they might return and shoot at us again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But eventually did you get out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. I looked around once again. Person number 32 also lifted his head, and we acknowledged each other. We exchanged questions. We asked each other whether we had been wounded, and then we said that we were going.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see the other men with you, who had been shot at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Right in front of us, Hasan Mutapcic was lying down, who had been hit in the head, and the -- there was an exit wound on the lower right-hand side of his jaw. His teeth had been blown out when the bullet shot through.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what about the other men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The other men were lying in the water as well. There were five dead bodies there all in all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to jump ahead for a moment. In June of this year, the 26th of June, did you go back to the area with investigators from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you accompanied by, as we will see, members of the SFOR troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you asked to retrace your steps that day on the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was a video made of that trip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you've had an opportunity to look at that video.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask that the video be played. It's very short. It's about four minutes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. You've made arrangements with the audiovisual people?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we have and I'm going to ask the witness just to identify what we are looking at as we look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First of all, sir, what are we looking at here? Actually, think I just a moment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: It's not a very good picture. Yes. That's the house we were stopped in front of, with the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are we now looking towards the river Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, that's the road towards the Drina, and they stopped us in front of this house, that same house. This is the bank and the path towards the Drina. At that particular moment, potatoes had been sown in this field.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We are now, I think, looking back towards the house from the field.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: This is the place the crime took place at.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did it look like that in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, more or less, but there was less water. The water level was lower.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are we now looking back towards the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way. It's a small path and we moved along that path.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: This is the entrance to the hotel named Vilina Vlas.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did the hotel look like that in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where was Vasiljevic standing when you first saw him that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: On the left-hand side from the reception desk. To the left, looking at it, to the left of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Thank you. I think that's all we need. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, after you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you going to do something about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That shows how long it's been since I've been in court. Your Honour, may I ask that be marked an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand it's Exhibit 18, Prosecution Exhibit 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, none. I received the tape a few days ago from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P18. That's the number that's been assigned on the list, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well, P18.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, as required, a statement from the person who took them, actually made the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't know. Is that part of an agreement, or is it being tendered separately or what?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think I can leave that. I think it's by agreement, in any event, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But the tape has gone in without objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And it's been described by the witness. Do you need the statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm just -- I'm puzzled as to what we do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. It's just if there were to be any kind of a dispute, there is a statement. But as Your Honour says, it's been put in by agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Or without objection, anyway. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that you and Witness 32 both got out of the river. After that, did you return to -- I think, in fact, you went to your parents' house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. Except before that, from that place, we left for Musici.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were either you or Witness number 32 injured at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And eventually, as you told us earlier, did you join the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, in your statement, the one you gave to the investigator of the Prosecution, you mention at the very beginning that on the 11th of June, 1992, you became a member of the Visegrad Brigade, which at the start, until the fall of the town, was stationed in Visegrad first and then in Gorazde; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You also said that the brigade was reorganised later on to become the 851st Light Glorious, or famous, Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that a Muslim brigade? Was it made up of Muslims alone, or were there any Serbs in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No. They were only Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you explain, please, when you refer to the fall of the town, do you mean the point at which the Uzice Corps entered the town? Is that what you mean by "the fall"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your statement, it says that the brigade was in the town of Visegrad itself before the fall of Visegrad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But you've just confirmed that in your written statement you said that it was stationed in Visegrad until the fall of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: But Visegrad is a whole territory, so it wasn't stationed in the centre of town. It was at the periphery, on the outskirts, in a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know whether it was a regular army or a paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No. It was an organised brigade. Actually, it was the TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Domazet. We are having the usual problems about when you're both speaking the same language. Sir, when you are speaking the same language as counsel, it is very difficult for the interpreters to keep up because there is no pause while there is a translation going through. So after Mr. Domazet has asked his question, would you pause before you start the answer? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me go back for a moment to the day that you spoke about at length here today. But let me ask you first of all something else. I think you said today that it was Saturday, the 7th of June, 1992. That Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was the date you gave us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you quite sure that it was a Saturday, or are you more certain that it was the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, both. It was the 7th of June 1992, Saturday, and the time was 1730 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Although I don't consider this to be essential, that is not correct, because actually Sunday was the 7th, so Saturday could only have been the 6th of June. That is why I'm asking you are you more certain that it was a Saturday or a Sunday, or rather the 6th or the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The date was the 7th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So if I understand what you're saying, you're certain that it was the 7th of June. But that means that you're not quite sure whether it was a Saturday or Sunday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to ask you about the events in Bikavac and up to the arrival in Vilina Vlas except to ask you about a few points on which there is some difference between what you said today and the statement and what Witness VG32 said. So this is what I want to ask you: Could you tell us, please, what order did the vehicles proceed towards Banja? The Passat or the Yugo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The Passat went first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I assume that the Passat then arrived in front of the hotel at Visegradska Banja as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you sure? Because VG32 claims that the Yugo went ahead and reached Banja before the Passat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I can't guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you went towards the entrance of the hotel in Banja, who was the first person that you happened to notice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Momir Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he standing at the very entrance to the hotel, in front of the entrance? What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage uniform, a black hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say camouflage uniform, do you mean the camouflage uniform of the then JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. That uniform was worn by the former JNA. As you know they had an olive-green/grey uniform and a camouflage uniform depending on their assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with you there. I know that there was the olive-green uniform and that was uni-coloured, one coloured; is that right? And then there was the camouflage uniform, which, like all camouflage uniforms, was multi-coloured. So I'm asking you is it that type of camouflage uniform which the army used in addition to the olive-green/grey uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No. It was a blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you happen to know who used the blue camouflage uniform generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I didn't come across it previously, but I know that the police force wore that type of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: On that particular day, was Milan Lukic wearing that kind of camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think it was green.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You're not sure whether it was a blue camouflage uniform or the green-brown type of camouflage uniform? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: It was a blue uniform, and on the left shoulder, it said "police". And I think that that is recorded in the statement as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, I'm afraid I'm getting confused as to whether we are talking about the man standing outside the entrance to the hotel or Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we are speaking about other person. Momir Savic -- sorry, we are speaking about Milan Lukic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You can see how the confusion has arisen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, to avoid that, let's repeat. Momir Savic was wearing a camouflage uniform, but could you tell the Court again which type of camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: It was a green camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you again. Milan Lukic was also wearing a camouflage uniform, was he not? And you said that it had the police sign written upon it. What colour was his camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think it was the blue one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What uniform were the other two soldiers wearing who went with you from Bikavac to Vilina Vlas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: That young guy who came with Lukic to my flat was wearing the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. olive-green/grey uniform, and the other young man, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you talking about the two men who were with you in Vilina Vlas and on the banks of the Drina? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As you have said, they were differently dressed. Do you remember how the one who was in the Passat with you was dressed -- until you arrived at the Vilina Vlas hotel? How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I don't know which one you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I mean the soldier who was with you in the Passat vehicle, and of course Lukic, who was driving the Passat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think I said he was wearing the olive-green/grey uniform; the soldier who came with Lukic, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who was with Lukic and you in the Passat on your journey to Vilina Vlas; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You told us who you saw first and that it was Momir Savic before you went in to the reception desk. When you went into the reception hall, as you said a moment ago, on the left-hand side you saw Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, there is a door leading to the swimming pool, and then there is also a passageway. Can you tell us whether this was at the entrance to the pool -- there was a path. Was it at the entrance to the pool, or where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Between the path and the entrance to the pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your assessment, how far -- how great is the distance between that place and the path and the reception at the bottom of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Sir, you're going to great details. At that time, I was very afraid and excited, and I really can't measure in metres. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, sir, if my question disturbs you at all. I didn't mean to upset you. I know that you had no idea of measuring. But you were there two months ago again. We saw this on the video. And so I assumed that you could explain to us details of this kind. Let me repeat the question: Is the hall as big as this courtroom here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait a moment. It's 11.00. I should tell your co-counsel that his principal task in this trial is to make sure that you realise when we are coming up to the time for an adjournment. But Mr. Domazet my problem is this: What is all this about? We are told there is no real dispute about this. I know that you have been testing his memory about who was wearing what and what day of the week it was and everything, but that can be taken just so far. Are we going to see what different impression was made upon this man who doesn't suggest that he was a frequenter of this hotel like 32 was, what his impression was at this time, and what may have been refreshed two months ago? What does it do for us? How does it help us? It doesn't, insofar as I can see, assist in any way in judging his credit as a witness if he is or not able to give you these sorts of measurements. So when we resume at 11.30, may I suggest that we move on to what is in dispute? We will resume at 11.30. --- Break taken at 11.02 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, today you said to us that Mitar Vasiljevic had an automatic rifle on that day. When did you first actually see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: As soon as I saw Mitar, I saw the rifle as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So when you first saw him between the entrance into the pool and the reception desk, he had a rifle on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How was he holding the rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: He was holding it right next to him, like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You are showing this with your hand now. You're using your left hand and arm, and you're moving it downwards, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. But it wasn't in his left hand. It was in his right hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. But you used your left hand to show this, so that is why I said your left hand when describing it for the transcript. Was the rifle readily visible, in terms of the way in which he was carrying it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about the rest who were with you, including Witness VG32? Could they also see that rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, he did not see it; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember that in the statement you gave a few years ago to the investigator of the OTP, you said that Mitar Vasiljevic had a semi-automatic rifle? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's answer was not audible to the English booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you repeat that answer, please, sir? You were not heard by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you do not remember that you stated then that he had a semi-automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When leaving the Vilina Vlas Hotel, on the way to the car, did you notice a conversation taking place between Meho Dzafic and Mitar or, rather, that Meho asked Mitar for a cigarette and that Mitar gave him one and that Lukic reacted to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No, I did not notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When leaving Vilina Vlas by car, are you sure of the fact that the soldier who was with you in the Passat before then went into the Yugo rather than Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes. The soldier went into the Yugo, and Mitar Vasiljevic entered the Passat. He sat in the front seat next to Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: According to this statement of yours, in the Passat, there were still five of you and in the Yugo, there were six of them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As concerns Lukic, did you see him then for the first time at Bikavac when you were captured by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I knew Lukic, as I said in my statement, in my school days. However, when he went to Obrenovac, I did not see him. I had not seen him until the moment when he captured me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your written statement to the investigator, you said literally the following about Lukic - and I'm going to read this out to you and you'll tell me whether you still think so - "It seemed to me that Lukic was superior to the other Serbs. He did not ask anyone what to do with us, while the others put questions to him." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In view of what you noticed that day, concerning Lukic, would it have been possible for someone who was with him there to influence him and to make him change an order he would give?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: In my opinion, there was no such person around him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: A while ago, we saw a film. And also in your statement, you said that in the car by Sase, Milan Lukic asked Mitar Vasiljevic about a house, whether it was a Muslim house, and he got an affirmative answer to that. My question is whether that is the house that we saw on the film on the right-hand side when you look at it from the road, and is that where you stopped in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, that's the house, in front of which we stopped. However, I do not know whether it was a Muslim house or whether it was a Serb house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that that is the house that was referred to and in front of which you stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, that's the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In 1992, did it look the same way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No. It was covered in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that it had a different roof, or that it was covered by something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: The roof of the house was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said today that Milan Lukic was the man who ordered you to get out of the car and who ordered you all to walk towards the Drina? On that occasion, did he give orders to the effect that he wanted everyone to remain silent and that he didn't want anyone to say a word? Do you remember that kind of an order issued by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I do not remember any such order, but I do remember that he said that we shouldn't try to run away, because -- that they'd kill us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said today that Meho Dzafic asked Mitar for help at a given point in time. Was this at the moment when you were lined up along the bank of the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, it was at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At that moment, when you heard Meho Dzafic's words, did you hear somebody else's words, some other person from your group saying something similar to that or saying something to the effect that they should not kill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because Witness VG32 said that at that moment, Meho started moaning and he mentioned Mitar's name, but that Kurtalic also at that moment started speaking and that at that moment, the shooting started, and that interrupted what they were saying. Do you remember that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Or, rather, when anyone started to speak, anyone from that group, Meho included, did the shooting start straight away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Right after these words, the shooting started.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Witness VG32 maintains that Mitar Vasiljevic did not say a word throughout this time. Are you sure that he said something or that he had time to say anything in response to Meho Dzafic's plea?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I already mentioned during my testimony that after Meho Dzafic's plea, addressed to Mitar, not to kill him because they were colleagues from work, the other one answered him that he did not know him. That is the only conversation that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, this conversation was not heard by VG32. Was he in a position to hear it, if that conversation was taking place loudly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Sir, I can't tell you that because in that situation, my perception was -- I mean, perhaps we were not focused on that, listening to these conversations or whatever. We were thinking about our children who would be orphaned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I understand your response, but please do understand that there is a difference, a considerable difference at that, between what you have been saying about this and Witness VG32. I have been seeking an answer, and I'm not going to ask you anything else about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, it really doesn't help us to try and get this witness to say what he thinks of another witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm finished with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm glad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you explained to us that you are quite familiar with an automatic rifle, please explain the following to me and try to explain this to the Court as well: When you shoot individual gunshots, how fast can these gunshots come one after the another? How many bullets can be fired in succession and how fast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Sir, all of this depends on the man who is carrying the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me assume that it should be as fast as possible if you are pulling the trigger of the gun as fast as possible. What is the time that lapses between two gunshots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry, but these are provocative questions as far as I'm concerned, and they are pointless as far as our discussion is concerned. I'm not a military expert to calculate how fast ammunition is being fired or whatever, so could you please sidestep this issue altogether?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't ask you about this anymore, because I understood from what you said earlier on that you were very familiar with the way this automatic rifle works and that you could talk about it like any other person who was very familiar with such matters. So I'm not going to ask you anything else about this, but I'm just going to ask you whether you remember that in your previous statement to the investigator, you never mentioned the number of gunshots that you allegedly heard on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: No, nobody asked me about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, you remember that, and you said that today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Another question: After crossing the Drina River and going to your village, how much time did you spend in the village before you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: On all territories that were under the control of the then BH Army, I stayed for as long as this army would stay there. That is to say until my village fell, I stayed in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me remind you that you said that on the 11th of June - that is to say, four days after this event - you joined the Visegrad Brigade. Did that mean that you left the village, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: That does not mean that I left the village, because I could have been a member of the BH Army there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And what about Witness VG32? Did he stay in the village with you and for how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Yes, he was with me. He was staying at my family home, but I could not remember for how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would kindly ask that we try to agree on certain admitted facts with the Prosecutor that are included in the statement that he gave to the investigator so that we would not have to tender the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, the best procedure for this is for you to ask the Prosecution to agree that the particular passage upon which you rely appears in the B/C/S interpretation of the statement, and then the Prosecution either says yes or no, and accept -- that fact can be accepted. Then no documents have to be tendered. There is a problem - of course we have this in every case - that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the OTP's investigators take the statement from a witness in B/C/S, it's interpreted into English, and it is the English version which the witness signs. And then later on, somebody else interprets the English version back into B/C/S, which is the copy that you are given. Unfortunately, the B/C/S original does not always agree with what is put into the document that you receive. We've had this so often now that it's a wonder nobody's been able to resolve the problem about taking these statements. But all these happened too long ago. Anyway, you ask the Prosecution whether they accept the wording that -- upon which you rely appears in the B/C/S version of the statement, and we'll see what happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. I asked for your permission to ask the Prosecutor. These are only three specific matters. The first one is that in his statement of 1988 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You better give some references to the page number and paragraph number, if there is one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English version, page 584534, line 5 counting from the bottom. It says, "He had a semi-automatic rifle with him."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That statement was 1998, was it? You're recorded as having said 1988, but I think you said 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Sorry, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that passage accepted, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes? Your next passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 584535, line 17, where it says, "Lukic and Vasiljevic were walking on the right-hand side of this column."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is this again the English version that you're reading from?
