utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And what was the third one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The third one is actually -- there is actually nothing in the statement that confirms the number of gunshots. There is no such passage. Can we just agree on that, that nowhere in the statement does he say that he heard a certain number of shots?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That may take a moment to check, but we'll see how we go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, from looking at the paragraph dealing with this, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is that all, then, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, that's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet said he finished with the witness. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: I have a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Judge Janu has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Witness 32, you mentioned putting your trust into the Yugoslav National Army after you describe some actions which were done by White Eagles. And my question is: Did you or somebody else you know try to inform the local authorities about what is going on? For example, police? And if yes, what was the answer from this authority; and if no, why you didn't try to inform the official places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: I think that somewhere in my statement there is a comment about that. When Lukic took me off, my wife intervened on the same day. She went to the then command which was headquartered at the Bikavac Hotel. However, the answer they gave her was that they asked her which people had taken me off, which people had taken me away. And when she told them that they were these people with soot on their faces, they told my wife that they had no control over those people. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Was it the police station when she came to intervene or what place it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG14
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. It wasn't a police station, no. It was a command post of the then TO, Territorial Defence. How shall I explain this to you? It was a command post, the TO, the Territorial Defence, the Serb units that were put up at the Bikavac Hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, do you want to ask any questions arising out of Judge Janu's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How about you, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, sir, that now does finish your task here. We are very grateful to you for having come along to give your evidence and for the evidence which you have given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does that conclude your guest role, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It does. Fleeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls investigator Ib Jul Hansen. Your Honour, there are a couple of exhibits that aren't included in the binder. I'm going to ask our court person to distribute those to the Chamber now.

utterances.text: Thank you. You are, I understand, going to play this tape recording to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Well, is it the excerpts that are going to last one and three quarter hours that the Court Deputy was told?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME

utterances.text: Yes. Well, we may have to have a break somewhere along the line, depending at what time you want to play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So perhaps when we reach the hour, I will advise the Court of the -- I'll be referring to the portions in the transcript that the Court has in front of it now, and I also -- I will know how many minutes that the next section will be.

utterances.text: Sir, would you please make the solemn declaration in the document which the usher is showing you.

utterances.text: Would you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: My name is Ib Jul Hansen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you briefly describe for the Chamber your educational and professional background.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I'm a police officer. I joined the police force in 1969, and I have been an investigator since 1973.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that during the course of your over 30 years of police experience, you've investigated a number of different types of cases?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I would say almost all types of cases.

utterances.text: And did that investigative experience also include the investigation of criminal organisations and gangs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber when you first worked for the Office of the Prosecutor here at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I worked for OTP from 1995 until 1997, two years, as a seconded from my government, and then I left for another two years, and joined the Tribunal OTP again October 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And have you remained in the employment of the Office of the Prosecutor since that time?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The first time that you were at the Office of the Prosecutor, was there a predominant victim on the cases that you investigated? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I was investigating crimes in the aftermath of Operation Storm, which the Croats War in the -- or homeland war, so to speak. And I was at that time looking into what happened to the Serb victims and the Croat perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time in your -- during your second employment at the Office of the Prosecutor that you were assigned to the investigation or the case against Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It was December 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the course of your work on that case and subsequent to the arrest of Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic, did you participate in the interview of Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I participated in the interview of Mr. Vasiljevic that took place on the 17th -- 16th and 17th November 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did that take place?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It took place in this building, in a special room in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was present at that interview?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Present was the accused; Defence lawyer, Mr. Domazet; and Investigator Yves Roy; myself; you, sir; an interpreter; and a security guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was that interview conducted in compliance with the Rules of Procedure as they pertained to the interview of suspects?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the interview videotaped?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It was videotaped and audiotaped. I was tasked to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the accused advised of his right to remain silent?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: He was advised at the beginning of each day of his rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was he advised--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could there please be a pause between question and answer before the witness answers the question that is put.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's just the same, I'm afraid, as when the B/C/S counsel and the B/C/S witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the accused advised of his right to have an attorney present?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The accused was advised about this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And, in fact, his attorney was present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: He was present, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, I'm going to ask you -- I'm going to ask video now to play portions of that tape. And that is Prosecution number 15. And I'm going to -- after I stop the first tape, I'm going to ask you a few questions regarding it. I'd ask that the first portion of the tape be played at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can you tell us where we should have the transcript open?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The transcript I would refer you to, transcript -- the first transcript, page 11, line 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While they are queuing up the next section, Mr. Hansen, I would ask you is that a fair and accurate depiction of the interview that was conducted on the 16th of last year -- 16th of November last year?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the portion that we've just viewed, did that occur after he was -- Mr. Vasiljevic was advised of his rights under the Rules of Procedure of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. He was advised about his rights at the beginning of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the second section be played. And I would refer the Chamber to page 29, line 14. That's page 29, line 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: A few problems with the transcript there. One of them is significant -- or perhaps two of them. They refer in the transcript to "the SDA," where it was obviously "the SDS" that was said. And the next one, I think, was cured by something he'd said later, but I think at page 31, line 16, the answer as interpreted was, "were Serbs from Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, well, we will make those amendments to the -- to the transcript. I'll also just correct the record. I referred to this as Prosecution number 18. Prosecution number 18 was the written transcript. This is in fact the -- the tape itself is Prosecution number 22. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. So last, as we move to the next portion, I would refer Your Honours to page 33, at line 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would refer you for the next section to page 40, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a comment to make with respect to the transcript, the portion we've just heard. utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If there is some problem with that, we could get one of the interpreters to listen to this.

utterances.text: Your Honour, I will accept Mr. Domazet's representation regarding that, and we'll stipulate that the transcript be amended accordingly.

utterances.text: So, then, after the words "to the hospital," he may have the date the 14th of June, 1992.

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Was there something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he went to hospital, not when he left the hospital. When he went to hospital, not when he left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't recall having used the word -- I'm not recorded as having used the word "from the hospital" or "left the hospital." I used the words "to the hospital." Anyway, we know now what you say, Mr. Domazet. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would refer you for -- the next section would be page 40, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the next portion of the tape, I would refer the Chamber to page 43, line 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next portion of the videotape I would refer you to, page 50 at line 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next portion is the accused recounting the events at the Drina River and runs for approximately 15 minutes. Would you like --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll repeat that, Your Honour. The next portion of the video is where the accused recounts his version of what happened at the Drina River on the 7th of June, and runs approximately 15 minutes. Would the Court wish me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no, we will deal with that after the luncheon adjournment. But before we go, there are a couple of questions I'd like to ask you. What's happening about the agreed facts? We still haven't got a signed document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will be moving several items into evidence later today, and that will be one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The next -- seeing that it's been left so long, your response to Mr. Domazet's argument in his supplementary pre-trial brief, I think, better be put in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It has, Your Honour. It's been filed this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And finally, somebody - I don't know which party it is - keeps on suggesting to the Victims and Witnesses Section that a witness they want to call is an expert. And at the moment, I think it must be the Prosecution. And the Victims and Witnesses Section seems to think that this is a matter for the Trial Chamber to determine. I've never had to deal with this before. I don't know why the Victims and Witnesses Section have to know whether somebody is expert or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm aware of this, and I will investigate this and have an answer for the Court this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I hope the answer is we needn't worry about it. It seems to be way beyond our competence. Do they get some special treatment if they are an expert?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think experts receive a professional fee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, fees. Well, that's certainly something we are not concerned with. Very well, then. Well, if that's a good time to break, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. we will take the break now. We will resume at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.55 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I continue, I just want to correct the record. I inadvertently referred to the transcript as Exhibit number 18. It is in fact Exhibit number 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not even an exhibit yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, document 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the next portion of the video be played, and I'd refer Your Honours to page 53, line 22. It's 53, line 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next portion of the tape begins on your transcript page 83, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are we not going to go into the other questions that were asked? There were a series of questions asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If Your Honour wishes. Just in the interest of time, those are the edited portions the Prosecution wanted to enter. But I would be more than willing to continue to play the tape at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, no. I'm taking advantage of this to read the transcript, which we haven't seen before. But it's still -- if it goes into evidence, we will be able to look at it. Now, what was your next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The next page, Your Honour, will be page 83, line 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next excerpt is just on the very next page, page 85, and I draw your attention to line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask the video booth just to continue with the tape? The next few questions are germane. I'm not sure why we had instructed them to stop at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you tell them how far you want to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will cue him when we finish this section, Your Honour. I don't have the time stamp of when I want him to stop, but I will let him know. I propose we will go until page 89, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that we stop there and go to another section. Your Honour, the next section -- I'm referring to the second part of the transcript, and that's page 17, line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The second part? You mean the second day?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, the second -- the second transcript. We handed two sets of transcripts, and they are -- the pagination begins again at 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next section I would refer Your Honours to is page 68, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the next section, I would refer Your Honours to page 70, line 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You must have a different pagination to us because the last one started on 69, not 68, and we are already well into page 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I'll see if I can get you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the proper reference now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How does it start?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It begins, Your Honour, with a question by me saying, "Okay. You mentioned earlier today about the [redacted]."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Page 70, line 30. All you've done is you've left out the reference, "Does he know anybody else by the same name?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes all of the video that the Prosecution seeks for the Court to listen to at this time. We will be moving it into evidence and -- as well as the transcript. I just want to ask a few more questions to the investigator regarding the video to lay a foundation before I enter it into evidence, or tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, have you been watching this video as it's played?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does it fairly and accurately represent the video interview -- videotaped interview of the accused that you participated in?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that were you responsible for video recording?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would tender Prosecution number 22 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the tape, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's the tape itself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we are talking about this tape with the conversation of Mitar Vasiljevic, then I have no objections to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's what we are talking about. It will be Exhibit P22. Now, have you got only an English transcript, or have you got a B/C/S one as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I only have an English one here in court today, Your Honour. And that is Exhibit number 15, which I would tender at this time subject to corrections to the transcript that Mr. Domazet and myself would agree by stipulation to some of which the Court has pointed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection to document 15, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The -- I have the translation into B/C/S, and the accused has it too. All I wish to note is that in the English text, there are some slight errors, so I will compare it with the B/C/S translation that I have for any additions, amendments, or whatever. But I don't think they are significant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if there any significant ones, you can discuss those with Mr. Groome and between you, you can agree. I must confess the American term "stipulate" always worries me. It has so many different meanings, I'm not sure which one is intended. However, if you agree between the two of you that it should be amended, the amendments will be made that will be P.15. There is no reference anywhere to the protected witnesses anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There were two, Your Honour, but I discussed them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is otherwise a public document. Perhaps you better work out where they should be redacted, for the purposes of it being a public document, and we can make the alteration later. Nobody is going to be reading it overnight, I should think, but we should have to know if we have to quote part of it. We should not be quoting somebody's name who should not be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I also point out that one of the people mentioned has the same name as one of the protected witnesses. I think that will become clear who that is later in the trial, but I would also point that out to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We've got two people who have the same name, Mr. Groome. utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, did there come a time when you went to Visegrad and examined the crime scenes involved in this case?

utterances.text: Yes. I've been to Visegrad several times. The first time was in November 2000. I don't know if -- if that's ...

utterances.text: I want to draw your attention -- did you go there on a particular date with a specific purpose of taking pictures of the area?

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.text: It was in June. It is more exact on the 26th of June this year, 2001.

utterances.text: And was there a professional photographer assigned to work with you on that day?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, there was a photographer from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: His name was -- is Zoran Lesic.

utterances.text: When you say volume 17, we have no volume 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I mean the index separator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, I'd ask you to look at what's on the ELMO now.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: You recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It is a burnt-out house on -- next to a creek in Visegrad, in Pionirska Street

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For the record, do you recall this house by the creek?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does it fairly -- this picture fairly and accurately represent how the house appeared to you on the day you were there participating in the taking of pictures?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, would I tender 17-5 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's a very different photograph to the one that's just been handed up to us. I'm not sure what the relevance of the one we've just been handed up --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think maybe they've been confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is the house by the creek, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They are both of the house by the creek. One is a closeup.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the one that's on the screen, it hasn't been shown on the video yet. But the one that's up on our screen, that is the one you want to tender and that is the house by the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are only two pictures that I'm introducing at this stage, and perhaps if you could be handed both of them at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The problem, as the Court Deputy points out, is has the wrong number on the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. That's also numbered 17-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise for the misnumbering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the photograph marked 17-5, Mr. Domazet, the one that has been shown on the ELMO even though it hasn't been shown on the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in your hand, you're holding -- I see that both these photographs have been -- are marked "The Houses of Demir Omeragic." Perhaps the houses were taken from different angles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you look under the -- if you press the button Video Evidence, you'll see that on the ELMO, one of those numbers, 17-5 - and that is the one that is being tendered - it has now finally got on to the video. Now, have you any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you are entitled to have a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: All the photographs were provided. I'd refer Mr. Domazet to Index number 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll provide Defence counsel with my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is the house by the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. That will be Exhibit P17.5. Now, you better somehow sort out what number we should give to the other one when you do tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could ask for the copies of the other one, and we'll check before we hand them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a couple of questions about this picture while it's up on the ELMO. Where is the creek in relation to the house here?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The creek is to the left of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I know that the house has been mostly destroyed. Would it be fair to say --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: And behind maybe. To the left and behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Behind the house from the view that we are seeing now.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's not the best angle to see where the creek is, because the creek -- in the creek, there are quite high trees, and we don't see the trees here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be fair to call this a view of the front of this house?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask now that Exhibit number 17-10 be placed on the ELMO. And I'm having some sent up to the Bench now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, I'd ask you to take a look at what has been marked as Prosecution 17-10, a photograph. I ask you, do you recognize what that is?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I do. It's the rear side of the house, facing the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this is the same house --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It is the same house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it a fair and accurate representation of the house as it appeared on the day that you were there?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. It -- it was late June, and that was the way the house looked at that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time I would tender Prosecution number 17-10 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be Exhibit P17.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that 17-3 be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, did there come a time when you participated in taking a photograph of the areas concerned in this case from a helicopter?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It was on the 1st of September this year, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to take a look at what is now 17-3 - it's on the ELMO - and ask you do you recognize what that is a picture of?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I do. It's a house by the creek in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does it fairly and accurately represent how the house on the creek appeared at the time you participated in the taking of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to take the pointer and I'm going to ask you to trace the creek for the Court, indicate where the creek is?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: This is where the creek is in the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would move Prosecution number 17-3 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but the one that has been handed up to us is not the same photograph as is being shown on the ELMO. It's from a different perspective or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry for the confusion, Your Honour. Has it been corrected? Is that the correct one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, this is now the same photograph. It's also noted as 17-3. Any objection to this, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. But we'd like to receive copies of that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's fair enough. That will be Exhibit P17.3. And is it true to say that that is Pioneer Street or whatever you like to call it, the one that's at the top of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen I'd ask you to identify --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't have the photo now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Put it back on the ELMO. Would you please indicate to the Court where Pionirska Street is on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, this is Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to indicate the two houses owned by the Memic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. family.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And just -- just so it's clear, I would ask you to indicate where the building depicted in the previous photograph is on that photograph, the house by the creek?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: This is the house by the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's still very difficult I'm sorry, when the pointer keeps moving. Let's look at the first of those houses that you want, the one with the awning at the front, that's fairly clear, and the one to the right, those are the two that are owned by that family?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness, are those the two that are owned by that family?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And the one on the right, does that consist of two buildings or one building? This is why I've been having trouble with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: As far as I remember it consists of one building only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is a somewhat smaller one than the one higher up?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally, Investigator Hansen, could you indicate where would the school be in relation to where this picture was -- what we see in this picture?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The small part of a concrete area is visible in the upper right corner, and this is a part of the playground in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally I'd ask that the exhibit Prosecution number 17-4 be placed on the ELMO. That is an A3-size photograph. Investigator Hansen, I'd ask you to take a look at Prosecution 17-4 photograph on the ELMO

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Tell us whether you recognise what's depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I recognise Pionirska Street going from the bottom of the photo to the top, on the right-hand side of the photo is seen the school, which is over here, and in the middle to left-hand side of the photo is the house by the creek and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is this -- sorry, continue.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: And in all those trees to the left of that house is the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, is this one of the pictures that was taken from the helicopter during the mission that you participated in?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This photo was taken on the 1st of September this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does it fairly and accurately depict the scene as you saw it that day?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender Prosecution number 17-4 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It will be Exhibit P17.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, pursuant to your work on this case, did there come a time when you showed witnesses photo arrays?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to describe for the Court the procedure that you followed when you showed witnesses photo arrays?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: After the arrest of the accused, we got a photo of him and an array was made. It was an A3-size paper with 10 or 12 pictures on. Among those 10 or 12 pictures was one picture of the accused, and we showed those arrays to the witnesses we met and interviewed. The pictures showed were -- or the arrays showed were not always the same because we shuffled the pictures and so that the accused wasn't always, let's say, number 4, or number 7. We -- all the pictures were changed from time to time so that the witnesses didn't look at the same array.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the following document be put on the ELMO for demonstrative purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No signatures on it this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: This is an array with 12 pictures among -- among them is the picture of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is this an array that was actually shown to a witness or --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: This has never been shown to the witness because when a witness was shown one of those arrays, they were asked to sign on the person they pointed out and so did the investigator, so did I. I signed with the date and my name. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen were they always the same 12 photographs, just rearranged?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Or did you have different ones?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Always the same?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that what we see on the ELMO now is what one of the witnesses would have been presented with when you conducted this procedure?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm Going to ask now that the witness be shown what Prosecution is calling number 55VG78. Your Honour, for the purposes of clarity we will put a suffix on to the exhibit indicating which protected witness was shown which photo array, if that's acceptable to the Court, so VG78 would be VG78 would be what was shown to witness 78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you say a suffix, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The number coming after 55; so 55 dash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask to you take a look at VG78.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that it not be placed on the ELMO but just shown to the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, do you recognize what VG -- Prosecution number 55VG78 is?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is the photo array.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without saying the name, please?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Shown for Witness VG78 on the 23rd of January this year, 2001. And the witness signed the array. She even wrote the name of the accused at the top. And I also signed, or initialled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'd ask that the witness be shown Prosecution number 55VG87.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Investigator Hansen, do you recognize what you have just been shown?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a -- the photo array shown for Witness VG87 on the 18th of January -- on the 18th of January this year. It was signed by the witness, who also wrote his name on the top of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we've got the idea. Are you going to tender them through the witnesses when they're called, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What I'm going to propose is that I tender colour copies. I brought the originals into court for the Court to view and for Mr. Domazet to view. I'll actually be tendering colour copies of the actual documents that were shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: At the time when the witnesses are called?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will tender them in -- all through this witness here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we might do that when we resume. May I say that we are very grateful for being given a list of the witnesses for this week so far in advance. I've never had service like it before in my life in this Tribunal. I note, however, that there has been a typographical error found, so that the last of the witnesses, his pseudonym is VG21. And we will note that accordingly on our copies. We will resume again on Monday. Hopefully next week we might be able to sit through some time on Friday if we are not progressing fast enough through this list. But other than that, is there anything else you want to raise before we adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one thing, Your Honour. When we provided the exhibit binders, we were unclear how the Court intended to use them. We will be redoing them this weekend. If the Court has not made notes in them, and would like us, I think we can organise them in a way that they'll be a little easier for the Court to use next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that will be helpful. Certainly I have enough work this weekend not to read through all the exhibits. Really I don't read them until they are tendered, but you certainly may have them back. Mine are behind me if one of your large staff can pick them up. We will adjourn now until Monday at 9.30.
